jobs.subject: Mars — archives, galerie intérieure
jobs.prompt: Create ONE wide 16:9 environment-only master for a side-view 2D fighting stage, based closely on the supplied actual Mass Effect 3 Mars environment screenshot by its environment artist Neil McKnight. This is the interior circulation gallery of the Mars archives installation, not a new design. Preserve the reference's recognizable arrangement: low industrial ceiling with rectangular recessed panels and long dark steel cross-beams; massive slanted / chamfered wall ribs; muted rust-red vertical inset at the large left rib; warm dusty tan wall cavity and its pair of curved upright dark brackets; small angular waist-high equipment housing left of center; the very specific broad rounded-oblong doorway on the right opening onto another brown industrial gallery; thin rusty-red handrails along the right rear landing; dark metal floor panels with light edge strips. Match the restrained charcoal, taupe, dusty beige and dark rust palette and the warm shafts of light across the floor. Keep the same overall angle and architectural hierarchy as the source. Compose at fighter-height, slightly pull the camera back and lower it just enough that the existing gallery floor forms a continuous horizontal readable foreground band across the lower 24 percent of the frame. Keep stairs and the recessed service pit behind or below this foreground lane, and keep the existing right guardrail at the rear of the fighting plane. Do not replace the room with a generic hangar, laboratory, space panorama, decorative reactor, or a circular arena. No extra doors, no invented signage. No people, enemies, weapons, HUD, text, captions, logos, watermarks or border. Natural game-environment material detail, crisp high-resolution texture, controlled lighting, no painterly redesign or extreme cinematic depth blur. Output only a single finished flat background image, with opaque background.

jobs.subject: Kadara — marché
jobs.prompt: Create ONE wide 16:9 environment-only master for a 2D fighting stage that stays closely faithful to the supplied in-game environment image titled Kadara Market by BioWare environment artist Paul Haskins. Reconstruct this exact Mass Effect Andromeda market location and angle, not an invented sci-fi bazaar. Preserve the distinctive stacked gray / dark teal angular market modules embedded among rough orange-brown shelf-like rocks; immense pitted rock overhangs high in the background; warm peach-orange backlit sky; cool cyan lighting from the left and right building windows; left-of-center tall narrow vertical street fixture with circular hoops; suspended black cables crossing the scene; broad dark navy canopy across the upper right with its pale curved emblem, with the black mesh awning immediately beneath it; compact irregular multicolored alien shop light shapes at middle distance; the middle-right metal ramp and its platform; the damp dark metal floor, scattered steam in the midground, and warm/cool lighting balance. Preserve the source's unusual architectural silhouettes, stall profiles and major color placements. Remove the people and ships so the environment can be reused behind fighters. Compose at approximately the same low viewpoint, but pull the camera back enough to reveal a level unobstructed foreground floor strip spanning the lower 25 percent of the image. Keep the reference crates and small props at the far left/right borders or behind the fighting lane, so no tall prop blocks the central foreground. Do not invent a new plaza, gothic domes, medieval market, dense vegetation or generic neon city. Keep signage as the source's small abstract luminous glyph clusters, no new readable words. No HUD, characters, captions, title, publisher logos, watermark or border. High-detail game-environment look matching the reference's materials; realistic geometry and perspective, not a painted reinterpretation. Output only the single finished flat background, opaque.

jobs.subject: Eos — caveau reliquat, salle de réactivation
jobs.prompt: Create ONE wide 16:9 environment-only master for a side-view 2D fighting stage, faithfully reconstructing the HEART / REACTIVATION CHAMBER of the EOS REMNANT VAULT in Mass Effect Andromeda, as shown in these two actual environment screenshots published by its level artist Jonathon Banks. Both references show the same chamber: use image 1 for the arrangement of the central polygonal floor dais and surrounding floor, image 2 only to clarify the shapes of the layered pyramidal machines and the huge chamber. Preserve the exceptionally specific Remnant architecture: dark blue-black laminated geometric blocks with countless thin irregular green-cyan circuit traces; enormous inverted stepped / sliced pyramids suspended from above; matching low pyramidal blocks around the sides; the central thin intense blue-white vertical energy column connecting the underside of the suspended machine to its angular polygonal floor receiver; broad slanted gray plates around that receiver; pools of dark blue-green ferrofluid outside the solid walkways; cold deep navy atmosphere and controlled cyan/green reflections. Do not add a ring-shaped portal, a glowing sphere, human machinery, a circular stadium, gothic architecture or unrelated alien structures. Reposition the viewpoint from the source's overhead inspection view to a lower, slightly elevated fighter-height view from the near platform edge, facing across the same room toward the energy column slightly right of center. Reveal a continuous broad segment of the existing dark stone/metal walkway as a level horizontal foreground lane across the lower 25 percent of the image. The central receiver and energy column stay BEHIND that foreground lane. Preserve the gaps and ferrofluid behind / beside the walkway; do not fill the chamber with an invented courtyard. Keep the large architectural scale and layered pyramid profiles immediately recognizable. No characters, enemies, HUD, words, captions, logos, watermarks or borders. Retain realistic in-game environmental materials and controlled dark mood while keeping the foreground floor contour readable, no stylized repaint or extreme bloom. Output a single opaque flat background image.

jobs.subject: Pragia — centre de recherche, salle envahie de végétation
jobs.prompt: Create ONE wide 16:9 environment-only master for a 2D fighting stage using the supplied actual Mass Effect 2 Pragia environment screenshot by level artist Neil McKnight as the exact visual reference. This is the abandoned Cerberus research facility from Jack's mission, specifically this overgrown tall interior room. Preserve the actual room layout and recognizable shapes: tall pale gray-green rectangular metal wall panels separated by narrow vertically grooved structural ribs; stained dark seams; left raised metal walkway with a thin railing; a short cluster of large angular box-like laboratory equipment cabinets left of center; the recess, crates and narrow ramp behind them; a massive glossy dark tree trunk rising on the right and a second trunk on the far left; tangled roots, creeping vines across the back wall, ferns at floor level and a dense dark canopy invading the broken roof; pale cloudy daylight shafts through holes overhead; fine rain falling through the roof; cracked uneven square floor slabs with small rubble and root traces. Keep the damp cool blue-gray/gray-green palette, the subdued exposure, light reflecting gently from wet bark and panels. Do not transform it into a lush open jungle, medieval ruin, greenhouse, new laboratory, or generic science fiction corridor. Preserve the source architecture proportions and arrangement. Pull the camera back slightly and square it toward the long wall, retaining shallow believable perspective, to reveal an uncluttered horizontal foreground strip of the existing tiled floor across the lower 24 percent. The big trees, cabinets, crates and thick roots stay behind that combat lane; small flat cracks and debris may remain on the floor. Remove all characters and combat effects. No HUD, titles, readable signage, captions, publisher logos, watermarks or borders. High-resolution game-environment detail matching the source, not a painterly concept or glossy redesign. Output only one finished opaque flat background.
